23.0.s.en: (1) The summoning of the leaders to hear the address

23.0.0.en: A long time: after the passing of several years.

23.0.1.en: Officers: the plural of "officer," meaning an overseer or a deputy of the people.

23.0.2.en: After a period of time, when the wars of Canaan had ended and Joshua had grown old, Joshua called the people and their leaders in order to give them his charge and bid them farewell in his old age. This gathering was most likely at the place where he lived, in Timnath-serah, or in Shiloh before the tabernacle of meeting. Here we notice the concern of the faithful servant Joshua to sum up his counsel to his children in a farewell address, as Moses did (Deut 29-31) and as Samuel did (1 Sam 12).

23.1.0.en: Joshua did not attribute the victories to himself but to the Lord, who gave them to the people and who fought for His people. He made them understand that he had divided the land among them by lot, according to the Lord's choice of the place of each tribe, so that they would not quarrel after his death, from the banks of the Jordan River in the east to the Mediterranean Sea in the west, as was explained before.

23.1.1.en: Be careful to offer counsel to those in your care, so that you encourage them to live with God and to stand firm in the faith. Fulfill what you feel God asks of you, and your heart will be at rest. Trust that He will help you in this striving of yours and will give you grace in the eyes of those around you.

23.2.0.en: Come not among these nations: do not mingle with them.

23.2.1.en: The Lord had promised them the land, and He Himself drives out its inhabitants from before them, but they must hold fast to carrying out God's commandments, which the prophet Moses taught them and wrote in his books. This shows us the importance of handing down the faith and Christian conduct from generation to generation according to God's commandment, without deviation to the right through excess and exaggeration, or to the left through neglecting them. The children of Israel did carry out Joshua's words at times, and they drove out some of the pagan peoples in the days of the Judges, but they were slack in driving out the others, so these peoples became a snare to them and drew them into the worship of idols.

23.3.0.en: They must not mingle with the pagan peoples who dwelt in the land before them, nor with those who remained among them, nor mention the names of their gods, lest they become attached to them by swearing by their names, or worship them, or bow down to them. Rather, they were to cleave to the Lord, as they had done during the days of Joshua's life among them.

23.4.0.en: Since the Lord drove out from before them strong and great nations, so that no man stood against them, let them know that God's help to man is the secret of man's strength. God multiplies the strength of one so that he chases a thousand; He is the One who works in us as long as we love Him and believe in Him as King and God.

23.4.1.en: Here the importance of encouragement appears, so make your tongue sweet and encouraging to those you deal with, so that you may strengthen their weakness and draw them to Christ.

23.5.0.en: He warns them against turning back from the way of the Lord and entering into relationships, dealings and intermarriage with the pagan peoples, for the mother is the child's first educator, and it is she who plants faith in him. If a person is careless in this, God withdraws His help from him, and these wicked people hunt him down for evil like a snare that Satan uses to trap him. Then the person suffers from the conduct and errors that the wicked plant in him, until they themselves turn into a wicked people whom God destroys, as He destroyed the pagans who were before them. So the stumbling that the pagans would cause the Jews is likened to a snare into which the prey falls, or a thorn in the eye that prevents it from seeing so that it goes astray, or a whip that inflicts very painful lashes on a person.

23.6.0.en: Joshua announced to them that he was near the end of his life on earth, as will happen to every person, assuring them that the Lord's counsels of blessing for them are true, as has been proven in practice by their victories and their possession of the land. His threat of punishment is also true if they turn away from God, until the matter ends in their destruction from the land if they persist in transgressing God's good commandments, betraying His covenant and turning to the worship of other gods; then God's wrath will move against them severely and they will be destroyed. This happened in the captivity of the children of Israel at the hands of Assyria and then Babylon.

23.6.1.en: The servant has one role to encourage the weak and another necessary role to warn the careless, so that he may hold to God's law and love. So do not hesitate to show the truth in the manner suited to each of those for whom you are responsible, so that you draw all to God and keep them away from evil.

23.6.2.en: The last message here is God's last message to the people through Joshua.

24.0.0.en: Shechem: the present-day city of Nablus. It lies on the west bank of the Jordan, in the portion of the western half-tribe of Manasseh (Map 5), and it has good spiritual memories:

24.0.1.en: 1- There God gave Abraham the first promise, and he built the first altar to the Lord (Gen 12:6, 7).

24.0.2.en: 2- There the blessings and the curses were read to the people from Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal.

24.0.3.en: 3- In it were buried the bones of Joseph, which they had carried with them at the Exodus from Egypt, when they entered the Promised Land (Josh 8:30-35).

24.0.4.en: 4- There Joshua read the law of the Lord to the people (ch. 8:30). The flood: the River Euphrates.

24.0.5.en: Joshua gathered the people a second time at Shechem with their leaders and representatives, and they came to a holy assembly in the presence of God to hear the message directed to them from the Lord through Joshua's tongue, in which Joshua reviewed their whole history with God and all His support of them, from the call of Abraham from beyond the River Euphrates in Iraq, to leave the worship of idols that his family practiced and turn to the worship of God.

24.1.0.en: God chose Abraham and brought him to the land of Canaan and gave him a blessed offspring through Isaac, whom He granted him in his old age. Isaac begot Jacob and Esau. Because Esau was occupied with material desires, God gave him Mount Seir, and he dwelt in it and turned away from the spiritual life with God, while Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt (Gen 45:9, 10; 46:2-10), so that God might train them in the spiritual life through humiliation and hardship, and then faith and trust.

24.2.0.en: Moses and Aaron came and struck Egypt with the ten plagues until Pharaoh allowed the people to go out. They went out and came to the Red Sea, and God parted it for them and drowned the Egyptians in it when they tried to pursue them in order to seize them.

24.3.0.en: And he put darkness between you and the Egyptians: so that God might protect His people crossing the Red Sea from the Egyptians who were following them, He moved the pillar of fire from before the children of Israel to behind them, and it separated the Egyptians from the children of Israel. By the power and size of the fire, the Egyptians' sight was blocked and they could no longer see the children of Israel, so the fire was like darkness until all the children of Israel had crossed and come out of the sea. God hid His people from Pharaoh until the children of Israel came to the wilderness of Sinai, and He was glorified in His care for them. When they came to the land of the Amorites, they took their land. God did not allow Balaam to curse them but made him bless them; Balak king of Moab had brought him to curse the children of Israel, and God delivered them from his hand (Num 22, 23, 24). Joshua's saying "your eyes have seen" refers to the elderly and the older ones among them who witnessed these events even as children with their fathers.

24.4.0.en: The land of the Amorites: it lies east of the Jordan River.

24.4.1.en: Then they crossed the Jordan, and their wars with the Canaanite peoples began, with the fighting against Jericho and their capture of it, and then the wars of the west bank of the Jordan, which lasted about seven years, and their victory in them.

24.5.1.en: Here God announces the fulfillment of His promise to Moses to send the hornets to help His people in their war against the enemies (Ex 23:28; Deut 7:20). He sent them before the children of Israel when they fought the Amorites east of the Jordan River, so the enemies feared and fled, and God's people did not need to use their weapons to drive out the enemies, since God drove them out of the land by the stings of the hornets. So they received their land ready for habitation, with its cities and its crops, to enjoy.

24.5.2.en: May you review God's works with you so that you thank Him for them and your faith is thereby confirmed, and you are reassured and rejoice in His care for you.

24.6.0.en: Because of the greatness of God's work with His people, they must fear Him and serve Him faithfully, and abandon the remnants of idol worship that they practiced on the journey through the wilderness and that their forefathers had practiced earlier in Iraq, by the River Euphrates, before God's call to Abraham, and reject the gods of the Amorites, whose lands the Lord gave them as an inheritance.

24.6.1.en: Joshua asks them whether they want to serve God or to leave Him and serve the idols. In this he stirs them up so that they decide to serve God and do not halt between the two ways, that is, the worship of God and the worship of idols. He set himself forth as an example, for he resolved that he and his household would serve God and not the idols.

24.6.2.en: It is good for the servant to be an example to those he serves, giving them the good example whose steps they follow.

24.7.s.en: (2) The people's covenant to serve God

24.7.0.en: The people answered that it was impossible for them to leave the worship of God after what He had done for them.

24.7.1.en: For He is the One who rescued them from the bondage of Pharaoh in Egypt, preserved them by miracles on the journey through the wilderness, saved them from their enemies, drove them out before them and gave them their land as an inheritance. Therefore they were determined to worship Him as their God.

24.8.0.en: Joshua wanted to make clear to them that the commitment to worship the Lord must be complete. It is not easy, because God is holy and jealous for His name, and He does not forgive those who betray Him, turn away from worshiping Him and turn to worship another; rather, He punishes them and destroys them if they do so, because He wants the whole heart and the whole intention, not a part of them. Joshua wanted his people to know the obligations of life with God so as to enjoy all His blessings, just as Christ asked us to count the cost, that is, to carry His cross behind us so that we may enjoy His care and be sons of the Kingdom.

24.9.0.en: The people affirmed to Joshua their adherence to the worship of God, with insistence and repetition. Joshua made them witnesses against themselves, and they testified. He asked them to put away the strange gods from among them, that is, the statues of the gods that they still kept in their houses, so that their hearts would be wholly directed to God, and they promised him to obey God. Our father Jacob did this when he returned from his uncle Laban: he buried them and got rid of them, proving his good intention in worshiping God (Gen 33:18-20; 35:2).

24.10.0.en: A statute and an ordinance: what is meant is commitment to the covenant, that is, worshiping God and obeying His commandments.

24.10.1.en: The book of the law of God: the Book of Joshua is considered an extension of the five books of the Law that Moses wrote, so it was also called the book of the law of God.

24.10.2.en: Joshua made a covenant between the people and God and bound them to obey this covenant, that is, to worship God. Joshua recorded these words in this book of his, that is, the Book of Joshua, as part of the divine Law. He set up a great stone that was there in the place, under the oak at Shechem, which is considered a holy place. The stone is a symbol of Christ, the Rock of Ages, on whom, if the house is founded, it will never fall, however great the storms and tempests.

24.11.1.en: Joshua made the stone, which had been present for the words and had heard them, a witness against the people so that they would be committed to worshiping God. Then Joshua sent the people away to their dwelling places.

24.11.2.en: Examine yourself to know the goal of your life and to measure your steps, whether you are walking toward it or deviating from it into many sins, and if you have deviated, return to God by repentance, that is, remind yourself every day of your goal, which is the love of God.

24.12.s.en: (3) The death of Joshua and Eleazar, and the bones of Joseph

24.12.1.en: After Joshua bade farewell to his people and gave them his final commandments, he died at the age of one hundred and twenty years and was buried in the land of his inheritance in the city of Timnath-heres, which lies in the portion of Ephraim (Map 12). These last verses were written by someone other than Joshua, most likely the prophet Samuel, the writer of the Book of Judges.

24.13.0.en: The people continued in the worship of God in the days of Joshua and in the days of the elders who were contemporary with him, who had witnessed God's work in the entering of the land, and whose lives were long after Joshua's death.

24.14.0.en: Piece of money: a coin whose value is not known.

24.14.1.en: The hill of Phinehas: the name of a city of the priests in the portion of the tribe of Ephraim.

24.14.2.en: Mount Gaash: a mountain near the city of Timnath-serah.

24.14.3.en: Joseph had died in Egypt and had charged the children of Israel to carry his bones with them when they went out. Joseph's death was more than two hundred years before Joshua's birth, so they took his bones when they went out and buried them in Shechem, the land that his father Jacob had earlier bought from the sons of Hamor when he returned to the land of Canaan from his uncle Laban (Gen 33:19).

24.15.0.en: Eleazar: a Hebrew name meaning "God helps."

24.15.1.en: Then Eleazar the high priest, the son of Aaron, died and was buried in the hill of Phinehas his son, which is one of the cities of the priests in the portion of the tribe of Ephraim.

24.15.2.en: We received the right to our heavenly inheritance when our High Priest Jesus died, our Leader on our journey, so let us thank God for this inheritance that does not perish and rejoice in it.

24.15.3.en: Joshua is a type of Christ. (1) He shares the name with Christ, for both names derive from "Yehoshua," which means the Lord is Savior. (2) The crossing: Joshua crossed with the people over the Jordan River when he parted it by the entry of the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and so he brought the people over to the new life in the Promised Land. Christ by His redemption brought us over from subjection to sin and the age of the Law to the new life with Him in His Church, in which we receive the sacrament of Baptism. As the people were baptized with Joshua in the Jordan, so we receive salvation in the sacrament of Baptism.

24.15.4.en: (3) The inheritance: as Joshua gave the land of Canaan and divided it among the tribes, so Christ gives us our eternal inheritance in the heavenly Canaan, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven.

24.15.5.en: (4) The commandments: Joshua was careful to charge his people to live with God and affirmed this in his farewell address at the end of the book, and Christ also gave His commandments so that His people might live by them.

24.15.6.en: (5) The covenant: Joshua made a covenant between God and His people before he died, so that they might live with God and keep His commandments, and Christ made a covenant between us and God by His blood on the cross, and gives us this covenant in His Church through its Holy Sacraments.

24.15.7.en: (6) Freedom: after Joshua charged his people, he left them free to choose the worship of God or the worship of idols, and they chose God. In the same way Christ also respected man's freedom and said, "He that hath ears to hear, let him hear" (Mt 11:15), or "Whoever wants to accept, let him accept."

24.15.8.en: (7) Miracles: God confirmed Joshua's teachings with miracles, such as the parting of the Jordan River (ch. 2) and the stopping of the sun and the moon during the fight against the enemies (ch. 10:12, 13). Christ confirmed His teachings with many miracles, such as healing the sick, raising the dead, casting out demons and His authority over nature. (8) The farewell address: Joshua gave his last instructions before his death in a farewell address at the end of the book, and Christ gave a farewell address to His disciples, which is recorded in (Jn 14-16). (9) Victory: Joshua triumphed over his enemies, whether in the wilderness of Sinai, as in his victory over Amalek (Ex 17), or in the land of Canaan, whose land he possessed, and Christ triumphed over Satan in the temptation on the mountain, then bound him by His cross and gave his place in heaven to those who believe in Him.
